content:
Fractions in Class 3 move on to equivalent fractions, comparing and fractions of a collection. This guide covers what the Maths Olympiad Class 3 fractions chapter tests, the key ideas, the comparison trap, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 3 Maths Olympiad Fractions chapter tests

  • Proper fractions (numerator/denominator)
  • Equivalent fractions
  • Comparing fractions (like and unlike)
  • Fraction of a collection and adding/subtracting like fractions

Key facts your child should know

  • Equivalent fractions show the same amount: 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6.
  • Same denominator → the bigger numerator wins (3/5 > 2/5).
  • Same numerator → the smaller denominator wins (1/3 > 1/4).
  • 1/3 of 12 = 12 ÷ 3 = 4; add like fractions by keeping the denominator (2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7).

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Comparing unlike fractions by numerator alone.
  • Changing the denominator when adding like fractions.
  • Confusing numerator and denominator.

quiz.title: IMO Class 3 Fractions Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: What must be added to 4/15 to get 11/15?
questions.explanation: Find the missing numerator: 11 − 4 = 7, so add 7/15.

questions.q: A box has 33 sweets. One-third of them are red. How many sweets are red?
A class has 30 students and one-third of them wear glasses. How many students wear glasses?
Which number is written at the bottom (the denominator) of the fraction 9/14?
questions.explanation: The bottom number of 9/14 is 14; that is its denominator.

questions.q: One-third of the plums in a basket is 21. How many plums are in the basket?
questions.explanation: If one-third is 21, the basket has 21 × 3 = 63 plums.

questions.q: Three of these are like fractions. Which one is NOT like the others: 5/12, 1/12, 11/12, 3/5?
questions.explanation: Like fractions share one denominator. Three of them have denominator 12, but 3/5 does not.

questions.q: When a whole is shared equally, which piece is smaller: 1/4 or 1/9?
questions.explanation: The more equal pieces you cut, the smaller each piece. So the fraction with the larger denominator is smaller: 1/9.

questions.q: In the fraction 5/9, what is the numerator?
questions.explanation: The number on top is the numerator, so it is 5.

questions.q: Among 1/3, 1/8, 1/12, which is the smallest piece of a whole?
questions.explanation: For unit fractions, a larger denominator gives the smallest piece, so 1/12 is the smallest.

faq.a: Different fractions that represent the same value, made by multiplying or dividing the top and bottom by the same number, e.g. 1/2 = 3/6.

faq.q: How do you compare fractions with the same numerator?
faq.a: The one with the smaller denominator is larger, because the whole is split into fewer, bigger parts.
